definitions.gloss: to be convinced; to be certain; to firmly believe
definitions.explanation: To have a strong, unwavering belief that something is true or will happen. Implies deep personal conviction based on evidence or intuition, stronger than simply 'thinking' something.

examples.japanese: {成功|せいこう}を{確信|かくしん}している。
{彼|かれ}の{無実|むじつ}を{確信|かくしん}していた。
examples.english: I was convinced of his innocence.

examples.japanese: {証拠|しょうこ}を{見|み}て、これは{間違|まちが}いないと{確信|かくしん}した。
examples.english: After seeing the evidence, I became certain that there was no mistake.

notes:
USAGE:
Expresses a stronger degree of certainty than {信|しん}じる (to believe). Often used when someone has strong grounds or evidence for their belief. The noun form {確信|かくしん} is also commonly used on its own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {確信|かくしん}を{持|も}つ (to have conviction)
- {確信|かくしん}を{得|え}る (to gain conviction)
- {確信|かくしん}に{変|か}わる (to turn into conviction)
- {確信犯|かくしんはん} (person who acts with full awareness that their actions are wrong)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {信|しん}じる: to believe — broader and weaker; can include faith without evidence
- {確|たし}かめる: to confirm, to verify — the act of checking, not the state of believing
